findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate and cover the two direct `_run_git([...commit...])` recovery commits in event_append (_recover_from_unmerged L471-473, _recover_from_invalid_object L536-538): either route them through the maint-suppressed helpers or inject _AUTOMAINT_OFF into these call sites, so no lock-held commit charges a foreground repack to _GIT_TIMEOUT.
evidence: event_append.py:471-473 `retry = _with_transient_fault_retry(lambda: _run_git(["git", "-C", tracker, "commit", "-q", "--no-verify", "-m", commit_msg]))`
event_append.py:536-538 identical direct `_run_git([...commit...])` inside _recover_from_invalid_object
These call sites do NOT route through _git_commit/_git_commit_paths, so injecting _AUTOMAINT_OFF into those two helpers alone leaves them uncovered
Both execute under the same write lock and _GIT_TIMEOUT=30 as the primary commit
findings.finding: The plan's _AUTOMAINT_OFF suppression targets only event_commit_git._git_commit / _git_commit_paths, but event_append issues two further lock-held `git commit` invocations that bypass those helpers and remain exposed to the same 30s-bounded foreground repack: _recover_from_unmerged (event_append.py:471-473) and _recover_from_invalid_object (event_append.py:536-538) each call _run_git(["git","-C",tracker,"commit",...]) directly. These recovery commits run under the write lock at the same _GIT_TIMEOUT=30 and would trigger the identical `git maintenance run --auto` O(store) repack the RCA blames.
scenarios: A commit that fails and enters UU-recovery or invalid-object recovery on a mature store, where the retry commit's foreground repack again exceeds 30s and is SIGKILLed
findings.suggested_fix: Route the two recovery-retry commits through the same _AUTOMAINT_OFF-injected commit helper (or pass _AUTOMAINT_OFF into their _run_git argv), and add these two surfaces to the Fix Plan's enumeration of lock-held commit sites alongside _git_commit/_git_commit_paths and txn.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the compensating explicit `run_auto_maintenance` runs after EVERY lock-held commit surface that receives `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` (event_append's stage_and_commit, delete_events, and the batch commit), so suppression is never applied without a matching serialized re-invocation and loose-growth stays bounded on all surfaces.
evidence: Plan: 'inject `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` so the 30s covers only the commit' applies to both `_git_commit` and `_git_commit_paths'.
Plan: '`event_append`: after a successful lock-held commit, call `run_auto_maintenance` UNDER the write lock (… loose-growth still bounded)' — stated once, generically.

src/rebar/_store/event_append.py: three lock-held commit sites — stage_and_commit L195 (`_git_commit`), delete_events L137 (`_git_commit_paths`), _commit_prepared_batch_under_lock L272 (`_git_commit`).

ADR 0051 Decision: `--unset gc.auto` is kept specifically so 'repack still fires and bounds loose-object growth (WU-1's goal is preserved)' — suppressing auto-maint without a compensating explicit run regresses this.
findings.finding: The fix suppresses auto-maintenance (`_AUTOMAINT_OFF`) on the shared commit verbs but only generically promises the compensating explicit `run_auto_maintenance` call 'after a successful lock-held commit' in event_append; event_append has three distinct lock-held commit surfaces (stage_and_commit, delete_events via _git_commit_paths, and _commit_prepared_batch_under_lock), so any surface that suppresses maintenance without re-invoking it leaves loose-object growth unbounded.
scenarios: A batch write or a retention-prune delete commits with `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` set but no compensating `run_auto_maintenance`, so its commits never trigger a repack.
A store driven mostly through the batch/delete surfaces accumulates loose objects unbounded, reintroducing the growth WU-1/ADR 0051 bound.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the RCA's 'repack exceeds 30s on a mature store' claim in a measured object count / repack duration on the reproduced store, and reconcile that figure against ADR 0051's ~8s-at-40k / ~300k-object escape-hatch threshold — confirming the ADR's own precondition for adopting this deferred mechanism is actually met (or note the divergence and why).
evidence: ADR 0051 Rejected alternatives: 'Disable + serialized explicit git maintenance run … the most robust option … Not adopted now on cost/complexity grounds … It is the escape hatch if the foreground-pause ceiling is ever approached at scale.'
ADR 0051 Consequences table: ~8s foreground pause at ~40,000 loose objects (~0.2ms/object); '~300k+ objects for one foreground repack to risk LockTimeout … Today's stores are far below that.'
ADR 0051 Follow-up: migrate to disable-auto-maintenance + serialized explicit gc 'If a store grows large enough that the foreground pause becomes disruptive (approaching the lock-budget ceiling).'
Plan RCA asserts the repack 'on a mature store … exceeds 30s' but the plan text gives no object-count/profiling figure crossing the ADR's ~300k threshold.
findings.finding: The Fix Plan adopts the exact maintenance mechanism (disable auto-maintenance on the bounded commit + explicit serialized `git maintenance run --auto` under the write lock) that ADR 0051 evaluated and DEFERRED as an 'escape hatch' contingent on the store approaching the lock-budget/object-count ceiling, but the plan cites no measured object count / store size demonstrating that ADR-set precondition has been reached.
findings.location: Fix Plan (Phase 2) — run_auto_maintenance / _AUTOMAINT_OFF and the RCA 'mature store … exceeds 30s' claim
scenarios: The failing run's temporary/isolated store may be small; if the repack is not actually an O(store) blowup past the ADR's threshold, the true cause may be I/O contention (as moldavite-evasive-elephant classified the earlier occurrence) rather than a foreground-repack-exceeds-30s mechanism.
Adopting the ADR's deferred escape-hatch before its stated scale precondition is met introduces the extra code + maintenance-cadence complexity the ADR chose to avoid.
findings.suggested_fix: In the RCA/reproduction, record the loose-object count and the measured `git maintenance run --auto` duration on the store that timed out, and cite them against ADR 0051's performance table so the plan shows the foreground-pause ceiling is genuinely approached rather than assumed.

evidence: ADR 0051 Rejected alternatives: 'Disable + serialized explicit `git maintenance run --task=gc` under the write lock — the most robust option and git-upstream's steer ... Not adopted now on cost/complexity grounds ... It is the **escape hatch** if the foreground-pause ceiling is ever approached at scale.'
ADR 0051 Follow-up: 'migrate to disable-auto-maintenance + serialized explicit gc on a controlled cadence (tracked on bug 88eb)'

docs/concurrency.md: 'should migrate to disabled auto-maintenance + `git maintenance run --task=gc` serialized under the write lock out of band (the git-upstream / GitLab-Gitaly pattern; the ADR 0051 escape hatch)'
The plan cites ADR 0051 for the mechanism but does not note that ADR 0051 pre-analyzed this exact fix and deferred it, nor reference bug 88eb (88eb-2beb-65f5-4bc0).
findings.finding: The plan adopts a fix that ADR 0051 already analyzed and explicitly DEFERRED as an 'escape hatch'/'Follow-up' (disable auto-maintenance + serialized explicit git maintenance under the write lock), gated on a scaling ceiling, but the plan does not acknowledge this decision-of-record or its gating rationale, nor link to bug 88eb which tracks the follow-up.
findings.location: Fix Plan (Phase 2), 'Fix decouples maintenance from the latency-bounded commit'
scenarios: A reviewer/maintainer needs to reconcile whether adopting the escape hatch now is a deliberate reversal of ADR 0051's deferral (scaling ceiling reached?) or an oversight.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note to the Fix Plan that ADR 0051 already identified this approach as the most-robust option / git-upstream steer and deferred it as an escape hatch tracked on bug 88eb; record why it is being adopted now (correctness-forcing timeout failure, not the scaling ceiling) and update/cross-reference ADR 0051 + bug 88eb so the decision-of-record stays consistent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve why `run_auto_maintenance` uses `git maintenance run --auto` rather than the ADR-documented `--task=gc`, confirming it still triggers the repack and takes the object-db lock (or switch to the documented `--task=gc` form).
evidence: ADR 0051: escape hatch is 'serialized explicit `git maintenance run --task=gc` under the write lock ... (that command takes the object-db lock; the GitLab/Gitaly pattern)'

Plan specifies `git maintenance run --auto` (not `--task=gc`); the plan does not state whether `--auto` triggers the repack (it is gated on maintenance.auto thresholds) or takes the object-db lock equivalently.
findings.finding: The plan's `run_auto_maintenance` uses `git maintenance run --auto`, but the prior-art pattern documented in ADR 0051 / concurrency.md that makes serialized maintenance SAFE relies on `git maintenance run --task=gc` because that command 'takes the object-db lock'. Whether `--auto` performs the equivalent repack and lock acquisition is an unresolved capability assertion.
scenarios: If `--auto` no-ops because the plan's own `_AUTOMAINT_OFF`/config leaves maintenance.auto disabled, or if it does not repack, loose-object growth is no longer bounded — regressing WU-1's goal.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether ADR 0051 (or an equivalent design note) is updated to record the new decoupled-maintenance pattern (_AUTOMAINT_OFF on the bounded commit + explicit run_auto_maintenance under the lock).
evidence: 'on git >=2.47 the lock-held git commit runs git maintenance run --auto FOREGROUND (ADR 0051)'
'call run_auto_maintenance UNDER the write lock (ADR 0051 serialization preserved)'
Absence: no bullet or AC states ADR 0051 is updated to document _AUTOMAINT_OFF + explicit post-commit maintenance as the new pattern
findings.finding: The fix changes the maintenance-timing contract that ADR 0051 describes (foreground auto-maintenance charged to the lock-held commit) by decoupling maintenance into an explicit `run_auto_maintenance` call plus an `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` suppression on the bounded commit, but the plan cites ADR 0051 only for preservation and does not state whether ADR 0051 (or an AGENTS.md/design note) must be updated to record the new decoupled-maintenance pattern.
scenarios: A future maintainer reads ADR 0051, expects foreground auto-maintenance inside the commit, and is surprised by the _AUTOMAINT_OFF suppression + separate explicit call
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bullet: update ADR 0051 to document that auto-maintenance is now suppressed on the latency-bounded commit and run explicitly under the lock via gitutil.run_auto_maintenance, so the recorded contract matches the code.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concurrent-writer latency expectation when run_auto_maintenance holds the write lock for up to _LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT (120s) on a mature store, or note why lock-held maintenance latency is acceptable under suite load.
evidence: 'call run_auto_maintenance UNDER the write lock ... loose-growth still bounded'
'bounded by watchdog-grade _LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT (120s)'
Absence: no statement of the effect on concurrent writers waiting on the lock during a lock-held 120s-bounded maintenance
findings.finding: The fix relocates the O(store) repack to run_auto_maintenance UNDER the write lock bounded at the 120s watchdog-grade timeout; since the originating bug was concurrent suite-load contention, the plan does not state the load expectation for concurrent writers blocked by a maintenance run that can now hold the write lock for up to 120s.
scenarios: Under the same suite-load concurrency that produced the original timeout, a mature store triggers auto-maintenance that holds the write lock for up to 120s, delaying other writers
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence noting that auto-maintenance under the lock is triggered only past the loose threshold and bounded at 120s, and that concurrent writers wait rather than fail — confirming this is acceptable versus the prior SIGKILL failure mode.
